symptom: Operators can see only a major Redis version and cannot independently confirm the managed build used for a security fix.
diagnostic-action: Record the resource SKU, region, reported major version, Service Health notices and maintenance history; use Azure Support when a resource-level build attestation is required.

symptom: A team needs to know whether scaling a Premium cache can interrupt clients or lose data.
diagnostic-action: Inspect tier, clustering, persistence, client retry policy and maintenance window; treat transient connection errors during scaling as a platform operation risk.

symptom: An AKS workload using a managed identity cannot establish Entra-authenticated access to a Balanced-tier cache.
diagnostic-action: Verify cache tier capability, identity assignment, data-access policy, token audience, TLS endpoint and token refresh rather than testing a static access key.

symptom: Creating a cluster-mode replication group with multiple shards and no replicas conflicts with automatic-failover settings.
diagnostic-action: Compare shard and replica counts with Multi-AZ and automatic-failover prerequisites before changing the application client.

symptom: A client attempts to use IAM authentication with an ElastiCache deployment shape or user configuration that does not meet IAM-auth prerequisites.
diagnostic-action: Verify engine/version, TLS, RBAC user authentication mode, SigV4 principal permissions and connection-token generation.

symptom: A client tries to refresh IAM authentication from inside a MULTI/EXEC transaction and receives an unsupported-operation result.
diagnostic-action: Refresh the short-lived IAM token and reauthenticate outside transactions; inspect pool lifetime so connections renew before token expiry.

symptom: Reading a Pro database data source after a Terraform provider upgrade triggers a provider nil-pointer panic.
diagnostic-action: Capture provider version and stack trace, compare with the last working provider, and pin or upgrade the provider; do not diagnose the Redis data plane.

symptom: Concurrent database operations surface a misleading maintenance-not-found error instead of the underlying API throttling or operation constraint.
diagnostic-action: Correlate Terraform logs with REST status codes, serialize conflicting database operations, and apply bounded backoff for retryable control-plane responses.

symptom: Terraform rejects percentage or non-integer dataset-size input expected by the user for a Redis Cloud resource.
diagnostic-action: Validate units and provider schema before plan; distinguish a provider input-model limitation from cache memory consumption.

symptom: A database data source treats query-performance-factor as required even though users expect it to be optional.
diagnostic-action: Inspect provider schema and state, compare provider releases, and avoid attributing Terraform planning failure to the Redis server.
